hints.title: Consecutive Value Pair Grouping
hints.text: A harmonious subsequence contains only two values that differ by exactly one. Since order does not matter for subsequences, can occurrences of adjacent values be combined?

hints.title: Adjacent Frequency Sum Invariant
hints.text: For any number x present in the array, if x plus one is also present, the maximum subsequence containing only x and x plus one has length equal to their combined frequencies.

hints.title: Single Pass Adjacent Sum Evaluation Procedure
hints.text: Tally the frequency of every number in a count mapping. Then iterate through each unique key. If key plus one exists in the mapping, compute the sum of their counts and update the overall maximum. Return the highest sum found.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N subsequences results in exponential time complexity and immediate memory exhaustion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting frequencies in a hash map takes O(N) time and O(N) space, checking key and key + 1 in O(1) per unique entry.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should emphasize why subsequence order is irrelevant and handle cases where no adjacent pairs exist by returning zero.
